blindSummary:
This country poses serious risk for trans visitors, with a sharp resort-versus-local split. Under the penal code and a religious-law framework, same-sex conduct is criminalised (up to 8 years, with 100 lashes available), and gender-nonconforming nationals face prosecution and social erasure; activists operate from exile (a 2024 shadow report to a UN human-rights treaty body documents ICCPR violations). BUT: the tourist resort islands operate as a legally distinct world - no LGBT tourist is documented as prosecuted on a resort; the risk concentrates in the capital and the local islands.

A resort-only visit carries far less risk than the national legal framework alone would suggest; any local-island contact raises it.
blindOutOfScope: The resort islands are de-facto insulated; what is assessed here is the national legal framework and local-island exposure.
blindSourceSummaries: Alternative report by an international human-rights foundation to the UN Human Rights Committee (June 2024) on this country's protection of LGBTQI+ rights under the ICCPR: prepared with local activists - documents legal and social context, evidence and testimony of rights violations, and ICCPR provisions potentially violated. Same-sex conduct is criminalised with religious-law-derived penalties.

Human-rights measurement research project's 2024 country summary: expert survey data - LGBTQIA+ people are among the groups most commonly identified as at risk of violations of empowerment rights; low scores on freedom of religion or belief (1.8/10), assembly (4.1) and expression (4.7).

A foreign government's 2020 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under the 2014 penal code and religious law; significant societal stigma; no LGBT-specific protections.

Decriminalisation news site (Sept 2015): coverage of a once permissive island country turning restrictive - two men (aged 56 and 27) arrested in their private home on a local island for homosexual activity; the 2014 penal code extended criminalisation beyond adherents of the state religion to everyone, potentially punishable by death; a local LGBT rights group warned that tourists could face similar threats.

UN human-rights office compilation report (March 2015) for this country's 2nd-cycle universal periodic review: treaty-body and special-procedures information including reservations to ICCPR/CEDAW/CRC and human-rights concerns.

The country's own UPR national report (April 2015): the government's submission - development achievements, the 2014 penal code, and its handling of first-cycle recommendations (89 accepted, 20 rejected).
blindTangential: Same-sex conduct criminalised (up to 8 years, 100 lashes available) — a direct risk for trans visitors with partners, and the operative law on any local island.
